requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the generator and analyzer from crashing when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. Two diagnostic sites in `TypeCollector` no longer read `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 985, 1077). Separately, every analyzer diagnostic now passes through a new filter (line 239, lines 1444-1450). The filter drops any diagnostic whose location is not a source tree of the current compilation. Three metadata-reference tests and two doc paragraphs are added.
story.why: For a type that comes from metadata, `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty, so indexing `[0]` throws `IndexOutOfRangeException`. That exception makes the generator emit nothing, so the consuming assembly ships without a resolver.
touches_beyond_requirement: The diagnostic filter at line 239 applies to every diagnostic `TypeCollector` reports, not only to metadata types. Any diagnostic whose location is null / `Location.None` is now silently dropped, even for types declared in source.
README.md and MsgPack004.md gain new user-facing paragraphs. They state that diagnostics for referenced types are reported by the defining project.
The issue names three crashing `[0]` sites. Only two are visibly changed; the third (issue's line 735) is not in the diff.
story.confidence_overview: High that the reported repro no longer crashes: the new tests compile the defining code to a real metadata image and check both generator diagnostics and the resolver hint name. Medium on completeness, because one of the three sites named in the issue is not touched in the visible diff. Lower confidence that the global diagnostic filter hides nothing that was previously reported.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic now uses a helper that returns null instead of indexing `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. A property from metadata therefore no longer throws at this site.

claims.text: The README and MsgPack004 docs add user-facing statements about how diagnostics for referenced types are reported. The requirement did not ask for this.

breaker.reason: Checked README.md lines 1639-1643 and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md lines 49-52 against REQ-2283: both files add user-facing documentation about referenced-assembly member diagnostics being reported only in the defining assembly, which was not requested in the issue.

claims.text: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic now uses `FirstOrDefault()`. This diagnostic is built unconditionally, even when `reportDiagnostic` is null, so it is the most likely site where the generator itself crashed.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs lines 1075-1081 and GenericsFormatterTests.cs line 603: MemberNeedsKey now uses item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() at line 1077, the Diagnostic instance is constructed before the accessibility check at line 1078 and before this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke at line 1080 (so it executes even when reportDiagnostic is null in the generator), and ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember exercises it via an unkeyed public property on a metadata generic struct.

claims.text: Diagnostics whose location is not in a syntax tree of the analyzed compilation are no longer reported. This applies to metadata types and also to any diagnostic created with a null location.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs lines 239 and 1444-1450: this.reportDiagnostic wraps reportAnalyzerDiagnostic in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which checks diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree). Both foreign syntax trees and null locations (which become Location.None where IsInSource is false) fail this check and are not reported, as exercised by ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember.

claims.text: The tests really exercise the metadata-only path and the requirement's expected outcome. They: emit the defining source to a PE image; reference it via `MetadataReference.CreateFromImage`; run the analyzer and generator verifier; assert that no warning-or-higher generator diagnostics appear (this would include CS8785); and assert that the resolver hint name is produced.
claims.requirement_quote: So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**.

breaker.reason: Checked GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 633-674: CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync emits defineSource to a MemoryStream PE image (line 667) and wraps it with MetadataReference.CreateFromImage (line 673); RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync runs VerifyCS.Test with that metadata reference (lines 638-648), runs CSharpGeneratorDriver directly (lines 653-655), asserts no Warning-or-higher diagnostics are produced (line 656), and asserts expectedResolverHintName is in the generated hint names (line 658).

claims.text: The record-struct test uses exactly the `Item<T>` / `Cmd` repro from the issue, with the latest language version.

breaker.reason: Checked GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 551-580: defineSource declares Lib.Item<T> and usageSource declares App.Cmd matching the issue repro types, and line 579 passes LanguageVersion.Latest.

claims.text: No public API, analyzer rule descriptors, or wire format are changed. The new members are private.

refusals.what: The analyzer now silently suppresses every diagnostic whose location is not in the current compilation, including those with no location.
refusals.why: This changes which analyzer warnings users see across all rules, not only for this bug. That is a user-visible analyzer behavior decision.

refusals.what: README and MsgPack004 docs assert a policy ('reported by the assembly that defines it') that the requirement did not ask for. The policy holds only if the defining project runs the analyzer.
refusals.why: This is a documentation commitment beyond the bug fix and may overstate the guarantee.

findings.description: Claim C1 disputed: While line 985 and GetPropertyIdentifierLocation at line 1434 replace DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] with FirstOrDefault(), neither named test exercises this path: ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference uses [Key(0)] at line 517 and ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference uses [property: Key(0)] at line 559, so intKey == null && stringKey == null at line 983 is always false and line 985 is never reached.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is `Location.None`, not just those for metadata types. Helpers like `GetIdentifierLocation`, `GetLocation`, and `GetParameterListLocation` can return null even for source types (e.g. a partial/synthesized member without matching syntax), so diagnostics that previously surfaced with no location may now be silently swallowed. It also only checks the primary location, ignoring additional locations.

The issue names three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (its lines 735, 1009, 1101); only two are changed in this diff. If the third, earlier site still indexes `[0]` and is reachable for metadata types, other shapes of referenced generic structs may still crash. That would include those that only the generator path hits, where `reportDiagnostic` is null and the filter does not help.

For a referenced type with an unkeyed public member, the consumer now gets no diagnostic and the generator proceeds. The docs say the defining project reports it, but that is only true if the defining project runs the MessagePack analyzer. A NuGet package built without it gives the consumer no warning about a type that may not serialize as expected.

`SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck` means the content of the generated resolver is never checked. The tests only check that the resolver exists (by hint name) and that no diagnostics appear, not that a formatter for `MyGenericStruct<int>` / `Item<int>` is produced correctly.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops any diagnostic whose Location is Location.None (because Location.None.IsInSource is false), even though Roslyn analyzers are permitted to report Location.None diagnostics and only forbid locations in a foreign SyntaxTree. Because it filters on IsInSource rather than checking whether the analyzed symbol belongs to this.compilation.Assembly, diagnostics on types declared in the current compilation are silently lost whenever a location helper returns null: for example, GetPropertyIdentifierLocation at line 1434 casts GetSyntax() as PropertyDeclarationSyntax, which returns null for positional record and record struct properties (whose syntax is ParameterSyntax), so BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull at line 985 on e.g. [property: Key((string)null!)] in source is silently swallowed; likewise, any diagnostic using GetParameterListLocation (line 1454) when method is null or implicitly declared is no longer reported.

out_of_scope.description: New section 'Generic types from referenced assemblies' documenting diagnostic-ownership behavior.
New section saying the analyzer only reports on members declared in the current project.
The global diagnostic filter (`ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`) changes reporting for all diagnostics. Replacing the `[0]` indexing alone would have fixed the crash.

Evidence took 72 of 218 changed code lines off the list (C4, C5: tests found passing in the real run, claim upheld by the breaker). 146 stay with the owner.
